outlook.statement: The Company is very positive that in the coming years, we will be able to show stronger results than before.
From steady ground, ambition rises. As Eastern India awakens, we step forward not in haste, but with purpose to shape a lasting presence in the region's next chapter.

West Bengal is entering an investment-led growth cycle supported by infrastructure, industrialisation and urbanisation; the Company is uniquely positioned to leverage its deep regional presence, trusted brand and local expertise to capture long-term opportunities.

Roadmap for 2026-2029 rests on two sequential, deliberately de-risked approach: first centring on internal asset monetisation to build a growth-ready balance sheet by 2026-27, then evaluating new land acquisitions and joint-venture opportunities funded by internally generated capital, with West Bengal as primary theatre of expansion.

Consciously moved upmarket, targeting an 80% residential / 20% commercial mix weighted toward the upper-mid and premium/luxury segments to capture rising purchasing power of IT, GCC and corporate workforce converging on Kolkata.
Targeting Net Zero Emission by 2050, the Company started implementing various strategies and technologies to minimize energy consumption and maximise energy efficiency.

The Company expects the residential real estate market to remain stable, supported by steady urbanization, rising household incomes, and continued government emphasis on infrastructure and housing-linked policy support. Premium and high-end housing is expected to continue attracting the greatest developer focus.

risks: Due to the project completion accounting system that the Company follows, the profit for the year may be inadequate, even though the Company would have recorded good booking value.
Normal product cycle of a project in real estate company is 4-6 years.
Global conflicts, volatile commodity cycles and shifting capital flows
Regulatory compliance requirements for delisting and listing obligations
Dependence on West Bengal market for primary expansion
Project execution delays and cost overruns
Macroeconomic conditions affecting real estate demand
Project execution relies heavily on manual labour, exposing timelines to workforce availability and rising wage costs following labour law changes introduced in November 2025
Inconsistent approval processes and regulatory frameworks across states causing project delays and cost overruns
Sustained price appreciation straining affordability for first-time and middle-income buyers, contributing to moderation in overall sales volumes
Developers slower to adopt PropTech, digital sales tools, and green building practices risk losing competitive ground
Interest rate movements, regulatory changes, project-level demand-supply balance, and availability of financing for developers and homebuyers
